title: The Nervous System Overview
content:
# The Nervous System Overview

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the organisation of the nervous system
- Explain the roles of the central and peripheral nervous systems
- Distinguish between sensory, relay, and motor neurones
- Describe the pathway of information through the nervous system

## Introduction

The **nervous system** allows the body to detect and respond to changes in the environment. It uses electrical impulses to carry information rapidly, enabling quick responses to stimuli. The nervous system works alongside the endocrine system to coordinate body activities.

## Key Concepts

### Organisation of the Nervous System

**The nervous system is divided into:**

1. **Central Nervous System (CNS)**
   - Brain
   - Spinal cord

2. **Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)**
   - All nerves outside the CNS
   - Connects CNS to rest of body

[DIAGRAM: Organisation chart of nervous system]

### The Central Nervous System (CNS)

**The brain:**
- Main coordination centre
- Processes sensory information
- Initiates voluntary responses
- Controls higher functions (thinking, memory)
- Protected by skull and meninges

**The spinal cord:**
- Connects brain to peripheral nerves
- Coordinates reflexes
- Relays information to and from brain
- Protected by vertebral column

### The Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)

**Contains:**
- Sensory neurones (carry impulses TO CNS)
- Motor neurones (carry impulses FROM CNS)
- Nerves (bundles of neurone fibres)

**Divided into:**

| Division | Function | Control |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Somatic | Controls skeletal muscles | Voluntary |
| Autonomic | Controls internal organs | Involuntary |

**Autonomic nervous system further divided into:**

| Division | Effect | Example |
|----------|--------|--------|
| Sympathetic | "Fight or flight" | Increases heart rate |
| Parasympathetic | "Rest and digest" | Decreases heart rate |

### Types of Neurones

**Three types of neurone:**

| Type | Function | Direction | Location |
|------|----------|-----------|----------|
| Sensory | Carries impulses from receptors to CNS | Receptor → CNS | PNS |
| Relay (interneurone) | Connects sensory to motor neurones | Within CNS | CNS |
| Motor | Carries impulses from CNS to effectors | CNS → Effector | PNS |

[DIAGRAM: The three types of neurones showing structure]

### The Information Pathway

**Sequence of events:**

```
Stimulus (change in environment)
         ↓
Receptor (detects stimulus)
         ↓
Sensory neurone (carries impulse to CNS)
         ↓
Relay neurone (processes in CNS)
         ↓
Motor neurone (carries impulse to effector)
         ↓
Effector (muscle or gland)
         ↓
Response (action taken)
```

**Example: Touching a hot object**
1. Heat detected by thermoreceptors in skin
2. Sensory neurone carries impulse to spinal cord
3. Relay neurone passes impulse to motor neurone
4. Motor neurone carries impulse to arm muscles
5. Muscles contract, pulling hand away

### Receptors

**Receptors** are cells or structures that detect stimuli.

| Receptor type | Detects | Location |
|--------------|---------|----------|
| Photoreceptors | Light | Eye (retina) |
| Thermoreceptors | Temperature | Skin, hypothalamus |
| Chemoreceptors | Chemicals | Tongue, nose, blood vessels |
| Mechanoreceptors | Pressure/touch | Skin, ears |
| Pain receptors | Damage | Throughout body |
| Proprioceptors | Body position | Muscles, joints |

### Effectors

**Effectors** are structures that carry out responses.

| Type | What they do | Examples |
|------|-------------|----------|
| Muscles | Contract to cause movement | Skeletal, cardiac, smooth |
| Glands | Secrete substances | Sweat glands, endocrine glands |

### Voluntary vs Involuntary Responses

| Feature | Voluntary | Involuntary |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Conscious control | Yes | No |
| Thinking required | Yes | No |
| Speed | Slower | Faster |
| Pathway | Involves brain | May bypass brain |
| Example | Picking up a cup | Reflex withdrawal |

### Comparison: Nervous vs Endocrine Systems

| Feature | Nervous System | Endocrine System |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| Signal type | Electrical impulses | Chemical hormones |
| Transmission | Via neurones | Via blood |
| Speed | Very fast (milliseconds) | Slower (seconds to minutes) |
| Duration | Short-lived | Longer-lasting |
| Target | Specific organs | Can be widespread |
| Response | Immediate | May be delayed |

**Both systems work together** for effective coordination.

### The Role of the Brain

**Main areas and functions:**

| Area | Function |
|------|----------|
| Cerebrum | Conscious thought, memory, voluntary movement |
| Cerebellum | Balance, coordination, posture |
| Medulla | Heart rate, breathing, blood pressure |
| Hypothalamus | Temperature regulation, hunger, thirst |
| Pituitary | Hormone release (master gland) |

[DIAGRAM: Side view of brain showing main areas]

## Common Exam Questions

- Describe the pathway of a nerve impulse from stimulus to response
- Compare sensory and motor neurones
- Explain the difference between the CNS and PNS
- Compare voluntary and involuntary responses

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** Nerves and neurones are the same thing
- **Reality:** Neurones are individual cells; nerves are bundles of neurone fibres

- **Misconception:** The brain controls all responses
- **Reality:** Some reflexes are coordinated by the spinal cord alone

- **Misconception:** Sensory neurones only respond to touch
- **Reality:** Different sensory neurones detect different stimuli (light, sound, etc.)

- **Misconception:** The nervous system works independently
- **Reality:** It works closely with the endocrine system

## Practice Questions

1. Name the two parts of the central nervous system. (2 marks)

2. State the function of sensory neurones. (1 mark)

3. Describe the pathway of a nerve impulse when you touch something hot. (4 marks)

4. Compare the roles of sensory, relay, and motor neurones. (3 marks)

5. Explain two differences between the nervous system and the endocrine system. (4 marks)

6. A person sees a ball coming towards them and catches it. Describe how the nervous system enables this response. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Central nervous system | Brain and spinal cord |
| Peripheral nervous system | Nerves connecting CNS to rest of body |
| Sensory neurone | Neurone carrying impulses from receptor to CNS |
| Relay neurone | Neurone connecting sensory to motor neurones in CNS |
| Motor neurone | Neurone carrying impulses from CNS to effector |
| Receptor | Cell that detects stimuli |
| Effector | Muscle or gland that carries out response |
| Stimulus | Change in environment that triggers response |
| Impulse | Electrical signal transmitted along neurone |

## Summary

- Nervous system divided into CNS (brain + spinal cord) and PNS (peripheral nerves)
- Three types of neurones: sensory, relay, and motor
- Information pathway: stimulus → receptor → sensory → relay → motor → effector → response
- Receptors detect stimuli; effectors carry out responses
- Voluntary responses involve conscious thought; involuntary are automatic
- Nervous system is fast but short-lived; endocrine is slower but longer-lasting
